summary: Rabbi Tawil explores the laws and mindset of a mourner, focusing specifically on the prohibition of wearing tefillin on the first day of mourning. He examines the parallels between the seven days of mourning and the seven days of marriage established by Moshe Rabbenu, and analyzes the sources and reasoning behind when an Abel must put on tefillin.
questions: Why is a mourner prohibited from putting on tefillin on the first day?
What are the parallels between the seven days of mourning and the seven days of marriage?
When do the laws of tefillin apply to an Abel after the first day?
How does the timing of death and burial affect the obligation of tefillin on the first day?
